text:
The Wild arrive in Salt Lake City to close a five-game road trip, riding a 4-2 win at VAN two days ago that left the Canucks winless in ten (0-9-1). MIN is 3-1-1 in its last five, without Marcus Foligno and Nick Foligno, and it's the third game in four nights. UTA is 3-2-0 in its last five. Three days ago the Mammoth came back from two goals down to beat TBL 5-4 in overtime, with Dmitri Simashev scoring his first NHL goal to win it. They're missing John Marino; Andrew Peeke has moved up to 19:32 a night from 14:46.

On chances, our numbers see little between them at five on five: MIN has taken 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, UTA 58%. The Wild are better than their record, a +11 goal difference on +17.8 expected. UTA has taken 4.2 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays.

The goalies decide plenty. Projected starter Jesper Wallstedt (MIN) is at +7.9 goals saved above expected this season, while projected UTA starter Karel Vejmelka sits at -3.8 and has struggled over his last five starts, .843 and 6.5 goals worse than expected.

Kirill Kaprizov has a 50% chance to score, our highest on the board, and was drafted 135th overall in 2015. Dylan Guenther, who scored a power-play goal on Saturday, tops UTA at 32%.
